description: complete C++ tick-to-trade hot path measurement: Layer 0 (adjacency matrix construction) + Layer 1 (commutator) + Layer 2 (centroid lookup, K=100) + Layer 4 (decision table), single fused measured call per tick

layer0_cost_isolated.note: Layer 0 (adjacency matrix construction, O(N^2) with division per element) adds roughly 0.32us versus the Layer1+2-only fused measurement

not_measured: network ingest (DOCA/BlueField DPU parsing of raw ITCH/FIX/MBO packets into the dV/P input arrays) is not implemented or measured; this is the one remaining component of the specification's full tick-to-trade path that requires actual DPU hardware
order submission / FIX message formatting to the broker after the decision is made is not implemented or measured
tail_latency_note: p999 (9.05us) is roughly 4.6x the mean and grew relative to the Layer1+2-only measurement's p999 (6.72us); consistent with more code surface area increasing exposure to OS scheduler jitter on this unpinned, non-real-time kernel; CPU affinity pinning and RT kernel patching remain outstanding before any of these tail figures should be treated as production-representative
conclusion: the full CPU-only hot path (excluding DPU network ingest and order-gateway submission) measures approximately 2.1us mean, 3.6us p99. This is roughly 2400x above the specification's sub-microsecond target even in this optimized, dependency-free C++ implementation, confirming that DPU-level network ingest and further hot-path optimization (or an even lower V_threshold / smaller working set) would be required to approach that target — not achievable through Layer 1-4 optimization alone
